lines.text: A low, constant buzzing hum down the line. Something is moving in the walls.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My whole house is infested! Bugs in the walls, the vents, the cereal — everywhere! I can't even walk through the kitchen.

choices.label: Get everyone and the pets outside.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: We're all out on the lawn. There's grandma, the kids, and the dog — and a LOT of bugs following us.

choices.label: Stay out, don't reenter — sending the team.
Seal the doors so they don't spread next door.
Just light a few hundred candles 🕯️

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: 742 Birchwood Road. We'll be on the lawn — the one cloud of bugs you can't miss. Please hurry!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Pest control en route to fumigate and clear the house. Keep everyone on the lawn until they call the all-clear.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A groan, like the world is too loud.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My head is about to explode! 🤯

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: HUGE migraine, man. I feel like throwing up.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Thank you for sending someone! 12 Pine Rd.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Ambulance en route. Aim for the toilet, just in case.

library.title: My cat is stuck on a tall tree

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An old oak, a tiny furious silhouette near the top, a worried owner below.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My cat is stuck on a tall tree and won't come down!

choices.label: Is the cat hurt, or just stubborn?
Let it live up there. New life.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Just stubborn. And judging me, honestly.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Corner of Maple and 3rd, the big tree.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Animal Control handles it — they coax the cat down, calm and quick.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A roar, then an impact you can feel through the phone. Car alarms, screaming, a voice shouting from the middle of the street, out of breath.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Oh my god — a plane just hit the tower!

choices.label: Are you clear of the falling debris?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Small plane, I'm not sure, I'm across the river!

choices.label: Stay Safe. I'm tracking your location.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Okay — thank you very much, pls hurry!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Fire crews and rescue rolling, ambulances right behind. Keep everyone back across the street — you gave them a clear scene to work.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Radio static, breaking glass, a siren drowned out by the roar of a crowd. An officer's voice cuts through, breathing hard.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Dispatch, this is Unit 12 — riot's gone out of control downtown. I need backup, NOW!

choices.label: Have you tried asking them nicely?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Crowd's over a hundred and they've taken the intersection. I'm not injured — I can't hold this alone!

choices.label: Hold your position, backup is inbound.
Fall back to a safe perimeter and wait.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Copy. Holding at 5th and Main — send everything you've got, fast!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Backup units rolling to 5th and Main. Hang on, Unit 12 — they're almost there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A panicked voice, drowning in numbers.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I can't pay my debt! 💸

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My student loan! They said I'm too young to work.

choices.label: Run away before it's too late! 😏

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I'm 12! What do I do?!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Go back to your toys, kiddo. And free the line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A hushed voice, curtains barely parted. Three in the morning, and the street outside should be empty.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: There are people loading boxes into a van across the street. No lights, no talking. They've been at it for an hour.

choices.label: Stay inside. Can you describe the van?
Maybe it's just a late move?
Go knock and ask what they're doing.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: White panel van, no plates I can see. And… some of the boxes have air holes. Why would a box need air holes?

choices.label: Keep watching from cover. Help is coming.
Get the cross streets and stay on the line.
Honk your horn to scare them off.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Corner of Calder and 14th. They're closing the doors — please, send someone before they drive off!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Patrol rolling, quiet approach. You kept the caller safe and gave them a van, a corner, and a reason to hurry.

library.title: There's a fire in my bathroom!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A scented candle, a towel, and a very bad decision, now spreading.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: There's a fire in my bathroom! It's climbing the towels!

choices.label: Close the door and get out. Don't fight it.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Door's closed, I'm in the hall.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Flat 7, 19 Sienna Road.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: One room lost, a building saved. Clean work. Trust ticks up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A very calm voice with very odd priorities.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I need bitcoins urgently! 🪙

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I want to buy a virtual kitten.

choices.label: You don't need bitcoins for that.
What are you gonna name it? 😏

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: George Cheddar Washington!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Great choice. Now please free the line.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 2 a.m. A whisper. Something about the undead.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I think I saw a zombie! 🧟

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: It's in front of me, eating rotten flesh!

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Atlanta, Georgia. PLEASE hurry!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: You actually send the Zombie Containment Unit. Atlanta can sleep again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in front of a screen of red, plunging charts. He dials a number he shouldn't.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I bought bitcoin and lost everything.

choices.label: Yikes. What are you gonna do?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I think I'll rob a bank.

choices.label: I'm going to have to send the police.
Can I come? I'm broke too.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: 80% for me, 20% for you?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I need therapy to get over this.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Patrol on the way. Good call.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Split screen: you at the console; on the other end, a kitchen vanishing into orange smoke.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My kitchen is on fire! 🔥

choices.label: Are you out of the house?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: WHAT?! This is an EMERGENCY!

choices.label: And emergencies are what we do 😎
Sorry. Are you out of the house?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: No, it's way too hot!

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I can't get out, it's too hot!

choices.label: Get out of the house NOW.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I need someone, please!

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: 989 Burb Street.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Sirens. The truck rounds the corner before the roof gives. The city breathes a little easier. Citizen trust ticks up. Clean.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: An anguished voice, echoing off bathroom tile. The camera, if there were one, would rather not come in.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: HELP! I'm out of toilet paper!

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I don't care.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I'm barefoot!

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Please, I pooped!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Nicely handled. Good judgment pays, and the city cracks a smile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A dim alley. Something small shuffles between the trash cans. The caller is not breathing easy.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I found a baby dinosaur!

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: That's what I thought too. Until now.

choices.label: Let's say I believe you… what breed?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: No, it's a baby! I think it's a T-REX. Maybe?

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: 18th, Jurassic St.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: 18th, Jurassic St.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: You send Dino Control. The jeep rolls out — only unit trained for a baby T-Rex.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My stove caught fire — the grease just went up! Flames are on the cabinets now!

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Stay calm. Do not throw water on a grease fire. Is anyone still inside the apartment?

decision.prompt: Before you send anyone, what's your priority question?

choices.label: Is anyone trapped or unable to get out?
choices.feedback: Knowing there are people inside changes the response priority.

choices.label: Get out now — how fast is it spreading?
Try to smother it with a lid or baking soda.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: It's climbing the wall — I can't put this out!

lines.speaker: caller

lines.speaker: operator
lines.text: Get low, get to her, and head for the nearest exit. Help is on the way.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: I'm whispering because I'm hiding. There's a robbery at the QuickMart on 5th and Main.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: I've got you. Are you safe right now?

How many of them, and are there weapons?
Patch in a hostage negotiator on standby.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: Two men, ski masks. One has a handgun on the cashier. The other's watching the door.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: They keep shouting about the safe. I'm behind the drinks fridge.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: An armed crime in progress requires POLICE — they're trained to respond to active threats and secure the scene.

lines.speaker: operator
lines.text: Get low, get to her, and head for the nearest exit. Help is on the way.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: A spreading structure fire — with a possible trapped resident — requires FIRE DEPT: suppression plus search-and-rescue.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: There's a group cutting across my land near the south fence. Six, maybe seven people, moving fast.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: Thank you for calling. Stay inside and keep your distance. Can you see them clearly?

decision.prompt: You need the right unit. What do you ask?

choices.label: Are they armed, or does anyone look hurt?
choices.feedback: Good situational read before you commit a unit.

choices.label: Go out and tell them to stop.
choices.feedback: Never send a civilian to confront a group — keep them safe.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: They're heading for the dry creek bed toward the highway.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: No weapons that I can see… but one of them is limping, the others are helping him along.

lines.speaker: operator
lines.text: Understood — possible injury. I'll flag it for the responding unit.

lines.speaker: rookie
lines.text: An unauthorized crossing on private land near the line is BORDER PATROL's jurisdiction — they coordinate the response and any medical needs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Off the clock. First badge in your pocket that says DISPATCHER. The title is small. The way people start looking at it isn't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ones who used to talk over you, who never bothered to learn your name — they hear what you do now, and something behind their eyes shifts. This kind of respect doesn't get handed to you. You answer for it, one call at a time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You don't say much. You don't have to. The badge doesn't need announcing — and for the first time, walking your own street, you don't shrink.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hold your head up. Let them look. You spent years being overlooked; tonight you take up your full size, and nobody argues.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Senior Dispatcher now. Word gets around a small city. A save you worked makes the local news — a voice on the line that kept someone here long enough for help to arrive.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The people who used to wave off the job — 'you just answer phones' — go quiet when it comes up now. They're starting to understand that the phone is the first thing that stands between a bad day and a funeral.

decision.prompt: The doubters are reconsidering. What sits with you?

choices.label: It's not about them. It's about whoever calls next.
Feels good to be seen for once.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Either way, the story travels further than you do. You go back to the board the next night the same as always — but the city's picture of you has quietly changed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Supervisor stripes. The job stops being an abstraction to the people around you the day an emergency lands on a street you know — and the calm voice that walked someone through it came from a room like yours.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ones who used to mock the work don't have jokes anymore. When it's their block, their worst minute, the person on the other end of the line is suddenly the most important voice in the world. They get it now.

decision.prompt: Respect earned the hard way. How do you meet it?

choices.label: Graciously. Everyone's someone's worst day eventually.
Let the work keep answering for you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No speeches, no I-told-you-so. Just the quiet arithmetic of a city learning what you're for. The doubt doesn't survive contact with a real emergency.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Commander. The higher you go, the heavier the nights. The calls you carry home now are the ones nobody else could hold. Respect at this rank isn't given — it's the residue of everything you didn't let fall apart.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The people who once thought this was easy work will never know the weight of a bad night on the board. That's the trade: they respect the title, and you carry what earns it in silence.

decision.prompt: The weight is real. How do you hold it?

choices.label: Set it down for the night. You did enough today.
Carry it. It's the price of being the one they trust.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You breathe. Tomorrow the board lights up again, and again you'll be the steady voice at the center of someone's chaos. That's not a job title anymore. It's who you became.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Chief Operator. A room at City Hall, your name read out loud with the word 'service' after it. Somewhere in the folding chairs sit people who once looked right through you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There's no version of this where they don't have to admit it now. The ones who doubted, who mocked, who never expected anything of you — they're clapping. Respect, finally, out loud and on the record.

decision.prompt: The recognition you never expected. What do you feel?

choices.label: Grateful. And a little proud. You allow yourself that.
Focused. The medal doesn't answer calls — you do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You take the applause, then you take the elevator back down to the floor. The praise is nice. The work is the point. But tonight, just for a moment, the room feels a little bigger.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Director of the center. Now there are new recruits who look at you the way you once looked at the people who seemed untouchable. The doubt that used to follow you has been replaced by something else entirely: aspiration.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ones who mocked the job are the ones telling the next generation to learn from you. Full circle — from overlooked to the standard other people measure themselves against. You earned this desk one call at a time.

decision.prompt: What do you pass on to the ones just starting?

choices.label: Stay on the line when everyone else would hang up.
Be the calm voice in someone's worst minute. That's the whole job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They hang on the words. Respect isn't something you chase anymore — it's the room you walk into. And it all started with picking up a phone nobody thought mattered.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A number you don't know. When you pick up, the voice is careful, low — a detective, off the record.

lines.speaker: detective
lines.text: That case file you kept building? Somebody upstairs finally read it. We're moving. Quietly. I wanted you to hear it from me first.

decision.prompt: The thing you documented is becoming real. What do you say?

choices.label: Tell me what you need. I'm in.
Keep my name out of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You hand over everything — dates, plates, the map you kept on your fridge. For the first time the quiet on Calder Street has someone official listening.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 'Understood,' the detective says. Your name stays off it, but the file does the talking. Sometimes that's the bravest way to be brave.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 'Yeah,' the detective says, not arguing. 'It did.' Then, quieter: 'Thanks for not letting it die.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A knock at your door you didn't order. The man on the other side doesn't introduce himself. He doesn't have to.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: We appreciate a dispatcher who knows when to look away. Keep doing that. It'd be a shame if you forgot how.

decision.prompt: He's on your doorstep. What do you do?

choices.label: Close the door. Don't say a word.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You shut the door and stand behind it a long time. The message landed anyway. That was the point.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He smiles like your words are cute. 'Sure you didn't.' The door clicks shut on his side, and the street is very quiet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You nod. He's gone before you finish. You just agreed to something without saying a single word — the cleanest kind of deal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mailbox day. Bills, a pizza menu, and one envelope with the university's crest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They found your new address. Universities always do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You open it by the mailboxes anyway. Suspense is for people with savings.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Installments start this month. Miss them, and the apartment's on the line.

lines.speaker: neighbor
lines.text: University crest? My cousin got one of those. He lives in his car now.

lines.speaker: neighbor
lines.text: Hang in there. If you move out, I call dibs on the parking spot.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Comforting, in the way a fire alarm is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Upstairs, you run the numbers twice. Same answer both times.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rent, shifts, groceries, and now this. The kitchen feels smaller.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It goes on the fridge, next to the shift schedule.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two papers that own your life now. At least they're organized.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Forty minutes on hold to hear 'non-negotiable', said very kindly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The installments stand. You pin the letter up anyway. Arguing was free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: First break of the shift. The vending machine hums like it knows things.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your stomach files a formal complaint.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: First rough call tonight? You've got the stare. We all get the stare.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Partner slides a coffee across the table. Break-room diplomacy.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: It doesn't get easier. You just get better at ten-minute recoveries.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: Step one: eat something. Trust the veteran.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Partner heads back. Three minutes left, one humming machine, one thin wallet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A bag of nuts. Not a meal — a rumor of one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Still, your hands stop shaking halfway through the next call.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A real plate, hot food, ten quiet minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You walk back to the console feeling like a person again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tap water in a paper cup. Free, cold, loud in an empty stomach.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere in your pocket, the money quietly survives.

library.title: A Text From an Old Friend

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Shift's over. Your locker sticks, your feet ache, your phone buzzes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A name you haven't seen since before the academy.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Is this still your number?? Heard you work the 911 lines now. That's insane.

decision.prompt: A name from before the academy.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Same you, then. Good. Do you actually say 'what's your emergency'?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Five years compressed into typing bubbles. They appear, vanish, appear again.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: I kept meaning to text. Then it was five years. How does that happen?

decision.prompt: Five years. How DOES that happen?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The typing bubble thinks about that for a long time.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Okay, enough nostalgia over text. There's a burger place near your station. Now?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The city already took most of your voice tonight. A little is left.

decision.prompt: An old friend, out of nowhere.

choices.label: Leave it on read. Too tired.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two burgers, one hour, five years covered.

lines.speaker: friend
lines.text: Same laugh. Knew it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You'd forgotten what off-duty felt like. It feels like this.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 'Soon.' A thumbs up comes back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: People say 'soon' a lot in this job. Some of them mean it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The message sits there, read and unanswered.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The city takes your voice all night. Sometimes there's none left over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The café near the station, the one open at weird hours for people with weird hours. Someone at the counter is reading the book you own two copies of.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: They always burn the espresso here. We keep coming anyway.

decision.prompt: They nod at the book in your hand — same cover.

choices.label: Two copies, actually. One to lend, one to keep.
I only read it on nights I can't sleep. So — often.
Don't tell me how it ends. I've stopped three times.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: A lender AND a keeper. Rare.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They set the book down like they've decided the conversation is worth more than the chapter.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Weird hours, huh. Let me guess — you're either a nurse or you're running from something.

decision.prompt: How much do you give away?

choices.label: 911 dispatch. I run TOWARD the something.
Little of both. It's a long story and cold coffee.
Let's just say I'm good in a crisis.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Then I'm safe. Good to know.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The barista calls the next order and doesn't call yours. The moment stretches, warm, waiting on you.

choices.label: 'Great book. Terrible espresso.' Stay and talk.
Nod politely and take your cup to go.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Okay, burnt espresso tastes better free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You trade a smile and a phone number scribbled on a napkin. The walk home feels shorter than the map says it is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Twenty minutes become forty — the book, the city, the espresso. No numbers exchanged, but this café keeps weird hours, and so do you both. You'll be back tomorrow. So will they.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You take the cup and the exit. Through the window, the reader turns a page. Maybe next time — you tell yourself, and almost believe it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Shift's over. The reminder goes off as you hang up the headset.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: First installment. Due by midnight.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Partner reads your face before you say a word. Occupational hazard.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: Student loans? I finished paying mine the year my kid started hers.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: Advice? Pay the ones that know your address.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bus home takes the long way. It always does when you're broke.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kitchen table. Portal open. The clock counts down to midnight, unhurried.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The number isn't big. It's just bigger than comfortable.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Paid. The balance barely notices.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But the apartment stays yours another month. That's the whole game.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A late fee and a red banner, stamped at 12:01.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the fine print, the word 'lien' appears for the first time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Night off. The city you only know by voice is out there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Night market across town, or your own block. The bus costs what it costs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the stop, a stranger shares the bench and a bag of chestnuts.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Night market tonight. Whole city goes. You look like you never go.

lines.speaker: stranger
lines.text: Try the dumpling stall by the stadium. Tell them the bench sent you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Headlights swing the corner. The bus kneels, doors open, fare box patient.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Good food, loud music, streets you've only seen as addresses.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dumplings are real. So is the crowd. You almost relax.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then, past the stadium: vans. Parked in a row, engines running at midnight.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You memorize a plate without deciding to. Old habit. New thread.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your block, your corner store, your couch.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The city stays a voice on a wire. Tonight, that's enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The group chat wakes up after months asleep. Forty-one messages in ten minutes.
